title: Reduce avoidable Sol native-tool round trips
hypothesis: Explicit dependency-aware batching guidance reduces model calls on bounded edits without weakening tagged-edit correctness or verification.
falsified_if: The treatment has any failed edit run, increases failed mutations, or does not reduce mean model calls by at least 20 percent versus the native control.

variants.system_prompt_append: Minimize model round trips without guessing across dependencies. In each response, call every independent tool whose arguments are already known. For a bounded change affecting a few existing files, skip update_plan unless the task genuinely has multiple independent workstreams. After inspection, batch non-overlapping tagged edits whose replacements are all known. Once edits succeed, combine known focused checks into one run command using && when later checks do not need model judgment. Do not split plan updates, edits, or redundant verification into separate model turns merely to narrate progress. Start a new tool round only when its arguments depend on results from the previous round.

deterministic_outcomes: tagged edits succeed without stale or failed mutations
decision_rule: Adopt the batching guidance if both variants remain 3/3, treatment mean model calls improves by at least 20 percent, no treatment run exceeds seven model calls, and failed mutations remain zero.
